title.hi: ब्रह्मा की पूजा कोई क्यों नहीं करता?
title.en: Why Does No One Worship Brahma?

planted_question.text: Why does no one worship Brahma, the creator?

line.hi: ब्रह्मा, जिन्होंने यह पूरी सृष्टि रची
line.en: Brahma, who created all of this

line.hi: विष्णु, जो इस सृष्टि को पालते हैं
line.en: Vishnu, who keeps the world alive
Shiva, the one who ends all things
a small white flower called Ketaki

creator_named.meaning: Brahma shown as the creator of the universe

three_gods.meaning: the three gods side by side: creator, keeper, destroyer

inside_brahma.meaning: Vishnu steps inside Brahma's body and sees worlds

lotus_exit.meaning: Brahma climbs out of Vishnu's navel on the lotus stalk

pillar_appears.meaning: an endless pillar of fire erupts between them

flower_falls.meaning: a Ketaki flower drifts down past the swan

flower_testifies.meaning: the flower lies in front of everyone

shiva_liar.meaning: Shiva points at Brahma and roars

trident_strikes.meaning: Shiva strikes the ground with the trident

no_worship_verdict.meaning: the verdict: no one will worship Brahma

daksha_watches.meaning: Daksha watches Shiva leave, burning with hate

beats.intent: question + the whole answer (gives it away: 'a lie', 'a flower', 'Shiva's verdict')
explains the three gods, then 'who is greater' (abstract; opens with 'let us start from the beginning', not a hook)
Brahma's challenge, Vishnu sees worlds inside him (116 words, one long description)
Brahma lost inside Vishnu, exits by the lotus (118 words; chapter has no bridge line)
'both showed their greatness' (back-reference), weapons, pillar, the bet. Pillar at 3:05, race only at 3:26
boar and swan race; flower falls
Brahma hears 'upper heights' and sees a way to win
the bargain: the flower agrees to lie
Vishnu admits defeat, the flower testifies (no bridge line after it)
pillar cracks, Shiva appears: 'Liar!' (names used, not re-introduced)
Shiva explains the jyotirlinga (lecture before the verdict)
verdict on Brahma and the flower = the real payoff, 35 s after the climax
154-word recap + moral + earlier episodes + Daksha set-up

problems_found: Teaser 22.7 s and it gives the answer away (lie, flower, Shiva's verdict): nothing left to wait for.
First 3 minutes are argument and description (B02-B05, 142 s). Pillar at 3:05, race at 3:26 (43%).
Every beat is 45-154 words (no short punches); B04/B05/B14 over 110 words.
No chapter hooks or bridge lines; reel B opens on 'both showed their greatness' and never says who 'both' are.
Climax B11 at 5:20, verdict (payoff) 35 s later, then 138 s (29%) of explanation, recap and outro.
Episode is 7.97 min: under the 8 min rule.

new_plan.change: Cold open on the endless pillar and a flower falling; ask 'the creator of everything, yet almost no temple: why?'. Do NOT say lie/flower/verdict.

Hook in the fight itself (weapons raised, gods backing away) and introduce Brahma/Vishnu/Shiva in one line each. Stakes by 0:45: if the two fight, creation itself breaks. Plant: 'that day one of them lost something forever'. Cut the two body-journeys from 85 s to ~50 s (short punch beats: 'a million worlds.' / 'he could not find the way out.'). Turn: Brahma lost inside Vishnu. Payoff: he climbs out on the lotus, humiliated. Bridge: 'and then, between them, fire split the sky.'

Hook: 'a pillar of fire with no top and no bottom' + one-line re-intro of Brahma (creator) and Vishnu (keeper) + the bet. Race starts by 0:25 of the chapter (~3:25 overall is replaced by ~3:20 with a full race and the flower by 4:00). Short beats for the dive and the climb; long beat for the bargain dialogue. Payoff: Vishnu bows, the flower testifies. Bridge: 'everyone believed it. Except the pillar.'

Hook: the pillar cracks, a voice says 'Liar!' (re-introduce Shiva, Brahma, the Ketaki flower in one line each). Shiva's jyotirlinga explanation trimmed to ~20 s BEFORE the crack is fully open. Climax = the verdict on Brahma; payoff within 20 s: 'that is why almost no temple worships Brahma, and the Ketaki is never offered to Shiva'. Recap <= 40 words. Bridge = Daksha watching + comment question + next-episode tease (<= 25 s).

rewrite.target: 15 + 165 + 170 + 165 = 515 s = 8.6 min = about 1,400 Hindi script words at 0.367 s/word; post-climax <= 70 s.
